| [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |

Descent is a fact of provenance that the transport clause supplies, not something the kind criterion must recover. [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission concerns the identity of a work, which [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md) keeps apart from the kind. Active, because it is read off the record's own texts. It does not say judges track descent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md) | The manuscript's thesis and the October thesis give rival answers to what survives, which come apart in both directions on the cases of the receiver objection, yet the record links them by `complements` and scopes the October thesis to a question its fidelity clause does not stay inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. On those cases [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s fidelity clause give opposite verdicts on what survived, yet the two are joined by `complements`, which says they answer different parts of one question and do not compete, and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) answers only [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md). Granted: it is a comparison of texts and of the record's relations. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-214](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-214.md) | The distribution-over-situations criterion compares each language's own listener posterior, so it needs no correspondence of alternative sets; that a literal rendering can fail it is the criterion detecting a lost implicature, and a target language may admit no rendering that passes | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-236](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md). The objection's worked case is right, and it shows the criterion rejecting a rendering that keeps the literal content and loses a scalar implicature. Active, because it is read off the criterion's form and checked by arithmetic. It does not say the model is right or that the criterion applies to poems. | Active |
| [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md) | The task-paired risk difference the record uses in place of Blackwell's order, D_Q = sup_q \|R_q(U) − R_τ(q)(V)\|, is a different quantity: it reduces each risk set to one number, needs the losses of paired tasks on one scale, and its absolute value counts improvement as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The absolute value makes D_Q symmetric, against [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md). Granted, because each point is elementary. It objects to [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) by undermining the measure meant to realize it, not [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s truth, and it does not say a decision term is unworkable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) v2 | The headline that translation changes global structure is either about contextuality, which has no case but a constructed one while the behavioural data show none, or about inconsistent connectedness, the ordinary context dependence the line says it goes beyond | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala ([LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)) find no contextuality in five kinds of behavioural data, and [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md) reports that 34 of 90 language systems signal too much to be contextual. If pragmatic data are noncontextual as a rule, [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s defeat condition is met by default; what is left to change is overlap consistency, which is the "trivial sense of contextuality" and is fixed by the local distributions. The only instance of the headline is the stipulated [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). Among the claims [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) is cited only by [CLAIM-041](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md), not by [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md). The objection is open; it does not say a contextual pragmatic data set cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md) v2 | No design in the programme includes an interlingual translation, and the defeat conditions are disjunctive, so English retellings and model chains could settle a thesis about what survives translation | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens). Every stimulus set the designs name is English, or names no language; Villon→Henley and Marot→Hofstadter never enter a design. It does not say intralingual results are irrelevant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) v2 | Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange connects the two claims. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md) says such an image can improve access. Either that effect is impossible, or judged access is not Blackwell informativeness, and then [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s standard is not the one [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)'s receiver and its defeat condition use. It meets the shape of [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, not its letter. It is distinct from [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md), which sets the analyst against the receiver: this sets the ideal receiver against an actual one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) v2 | The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The source term of D(τ) for Villon, Henley or Marot can only be a modern reading, and for a live interlingual case the source and target judges are different communities, so the distance confounds population with transport. [CLAIM-074](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md) says fidelity differs across interpreters, as a thesis; it is not applied to the tests. It does not say cross-population fidelity is meaningless. | Active |

Granted, because it is a reading of the record. It does not say footing cannot be measured. | Active |
| [CLAIM-229](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-229.md) | The footing, compensation and constitution theses ground on invented cases whose readings the assistant assigned, and the case filed for the proposition's non-necessity holds the words fixed, so it shows only insufficiency | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), [CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md), [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-084](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-084.md) list fictional cases in `grounds`, which [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) makes evidence, while the cases' own bodies say they show a possibility, and [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)'s defeat condition asks a rival to predict a variation nobody observed. [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md), filed as the necessity half of [CLAIM-061](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-061.md), keeps the words fixed, so it shows only that the proposition is not sufficient. | [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) v2 | Blackwell comparison needs the state each rendering is about, which natural texts do not supply, so a decision measure is fixed by whoever labels the state, and it orders translation procedures, not single renderings | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Testing Blackwell's order needs the joint law of the situation and the signal. For natural texts the situation is what interpretation recovers, so it comes from the stimulus design, the analyst's labels or the judges, and decision-relevant information is measured against whoever fixed it. An experiment is a family of distributions, one per state, so a single rendering of a single poem is not one. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s defeat condition, "one rendering is a garbling of another", is then not well typed. | [CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md) | On observed responses, a rendering that keeps the response distribution of each order of two framings within ε of the source's, under an outcome correspondence, keeps the observed order effect within 2ε, a bound identified from data, while the intertwining identity bounds it only through defects of an unidentified state model | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md). | [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md) v2 | The line's proposed quantities have no finite-data estimators, and its evidence that signalling is typical of language data rests on plug-in estimates from one or a few occurrences, which signal even when the true marginals agree | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and empirical lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it. The plug-in signalling of two empirical marginals is positive in expectation when the true marginals agree, so raw tables signal, and the contextual fraction is undefined on them. With one occurrence per context, a non-signalling rank-2 system gives Δ of 0, 2 or 4, with expectation 2: the values [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md) finds in 51 of the 90 systems behind [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md)'s "69 of the 90 systems signal". The data are author-assigned corpus senses, not judgements. Deficiency over text-valued renderings has no estimator. It does not say signalling is rare in pragmatic judgements, where order effects are themselves signalling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-237](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-237.md) | The first open problem of directed transport is not yet posed: a contextual model is a menu of incompatible experiments, and under the natural order on menus any state-independent classical simulation is dominated automatically, so what is open is only the converse or a deficiency bound | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. It narrows what is open; it does not close it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md) v2 | Many of the line's defeat conditions cannot in practice be met: the comparative ones are null results with no margin over an observable set the thesis may re-choose, and the possibility theses' are universal negatives that no finite study establishes | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange raises it, though [CASE-029](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-029.md) records the decision rules that were dropped. The observables are "not fixed in advance" ([CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md)). Granted: each point is read off the texts. It does not say the theses are false or untestable in principle. | Active |

What the objection gets right is that no finite study meets them, so the programme's experiments do not test these two theses; argument does. Active, because it is read off the rule. | Active |
| [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md) v2 | Read as description, the manuscript's thesis is close to true by definition; read as a criterion, it is a schema until the decision family Q is fixed, and its descriptive defeat condition can test neither reading | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. | [CLAIM-245](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-245.md) | Under Contextuality-by-Default, a deterministic context-wise recoding can make a noncontextual signalling source maximally contextual, or turn a contextual source into pure signalling, so per-content signalling is not monotone under such maps and the quantity to bound is joint overlap discrepancy | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. Two worked rank-2 systems answer [NOTE-654](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-654.md)'s open question negatively: [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md)'s per-content signalling can rise under deterministic recodings, once the source signals, and CbD contextuality can be created or removed by them. Granted, because the examples are elementary. It does not say [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) is wrong, which is about no-signalling models. | Active |
| [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) | The bearer of communicative identity reversed, from an operational object defined on observed responses to a kind that can outrun observation, and no turn argues the change; both stances stand in the record | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. It is [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s point for the bearer of identity rather than the receiver. [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) is a theory of what identity is, with a kind that "may be real while remaining indistinguishable" under the probes. | [CLAIM-248](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-248.md) v3 | A language model agreeing with humans in direction is weak evidence, because models are trained on human text about teasing and reproach and the founding stimuli are famous, and the language-model test bed's defeat condition fires only on a reversal | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. | [CLAIM-249](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-249.md) | Comparing characters across realizations needs one group identified on both, which is fixed only up to automorphism, and automorphisms permute the irreducible characters, so "the same character" is relative to a chosen correspondence: the collapse problem again, at the level of the symmetry group | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. To say a visual realization has the same character as a spoken one, the same group element must be named on both sides. Changing that identification by an automorphism α turns χ into χ∘α, and for the cyclic group of order 3 the automorphism g ↦ g² swaps the two nontrivial characters. The transformations the line studies form a semigroup, so the group is a symmetry group the analyst chooses, with its action on each medium fixed independently: [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s anchoring once more. Granted, because the argument is elementary. [CLAIM-132](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-132.md) and [TERM-041](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-041.md) hold neighbouring limits, not this one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md) | The account does not say which distinctions a translation ought to keep: it says how to tell which ones a rendering kept for stated tasks and receivers, and what ought to be kept is set by the purpose the translation serves | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the criterion horn of [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md). | [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md) v2 | The intertwining defects are defined on unobservable interpretive-state spaces, so they are not identified from judgement data, and the commutator identity bounds observed order effects only with a further, unstated readout-intertwining defect | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. What is observed is responses, and the identity reaches the observed order effect only through a readout defect between outcome spaces, which no draft names. It is distinct from [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which is about collapse: this is about identification. | Active |
| [CLAIM-256](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-256.md) | D_obs sums over source contexts only, so a target context outside the image of τ appears in no term: a rendering that adds a relation pays nothing, and a change of cover registers only as loss | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. L_obs and D_obs are sums over source contexts, so a target context that is not the image of one appears in no term. The line says interpreters add relations ([CLAIM-076](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-076.md)) and that a transport can add a distinction ([CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)), and D_obs is the one component with a formula ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)). Granted, because it is read off the definition. It does not say no other component could catch an addition, or that additions are distortions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md) | Approximate transports compose into a category only if the distortion obeys a triangle inequality and later kernels are nonexpansive, so the semigroup claim's "category or semigroup" holds for exact kernels, and for approximate ones only under those conditions | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [TERM-008](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-008.md)'s founding sense is a transport that gets "within some eps", and [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) makes fidelity graded. Kernels always compose, but the composite of an ε₁-transport and an ε₂-transport is an (ε₁ + ε₂)-transport only if the distortion obeys a triangle inequality and the second kernel is nonexpansive. In total variation both hold. [QUESTION-017](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-017.md) holds the triangle inequality open and does not tie it to the category claim. Granted, because it is elementary. It does not say the category claim fails for exact transports or in total variation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md) | Forbidding self-endorsement does not stop an operator from amplifying its own authority: once endorsement can carry authority more than one hop, reciprocal and cyclic endorsements recycle it, and only one-hop allocation within an epoch makes an operator's authority independent of its own endorsements | A2's own analysis of the owner's U2 design, conceded in the exchange and checked here. With damped recursive delegation (a PageRank-like fixed point), two operators that endorse each other pass authority back and forth, so each one's authority depends on its own outgoing endorsements even though neither endorses itself. With one-hop allocation from budgets fixed independently of outgoing endorsements, that dependence is exactly zero. No accounting rule removes the slower route: an operator can change its authority by changing what others endorse. | Active |
| [CLAIM-289](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-289.md) | Non-stochastic strings stay non-stochastic under total recursive models: their minimal randomness deficiency agrees with the finite-set one to within O(log n) in argument and value | The step that [THEORY-260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-260.md)'s promotion (version 2) names as the record's own: carrying [LIT-239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-239.md)'s non-stochastic strings, proved for finite-set models, to total recursive function models through Propositions B.1(b) and B.2(b) with Remark B.3. Remark B.3 asserts wholesale that every result of the paper extends to total functions up to a logarithmic term. This writes the extension out for this one result. It holds at O(log n) precision only, and does not reach [LIT-229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-229.md)'s sophistication, which is defined at constant precision. | Active |
| [CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md) | A positive-definite kernel's minimal realizations are unique up to a unitary, and two finite representation matrices with the same centred Gram matrix differ by a translation and an orthogonal map | The record's own proofs of two steps that [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) rests on and that its sources state without proof. (a) Jorgensen & Tian's Cor. 1.35: minimal realizations of a positive-definite kernel are unique up to a unitary. The book leaves this "as an exercise", and [NOTE-829](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-829.md) supplied the book's own proof of Thm 4.35, transferred. (b) The finite case that [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md) §5.3 states as known: XXᵀ = YYᵀ implies Y = XQ with Q orthogonal, with no assumption that the rows span R^d. With centring this becomes a translation and an orthogonal map. It does not say Q is unique, which fails when the rank is below d. | Active |
| [CLAIM-291](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-291.md) | The adjoint of a square-integrable integral operator is the integral operator with the conjugate-transposed kernel | The record's own step, written down in [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md) and marked there as not the Riesz article's, which covers matrices and bounded operators only. For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. So T is self-adjoint, when μ = ν, exactly when k(x,y) = k̄(y,x) almost everywhere. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-292](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-292.md) | Retrieval that depends on current belief is not a bias in itself: adaptive search can be rational when inference accounts for how the evidence was selected, and calling a search biased needs a standard outside the search | Granted against [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md), as A21 insisted ("That counter is essential. Without it, we'd be using 'anchoring' as a blanket criticism of adaptive search."), and said again at A20 §5, A21 §4 and A23 V.E. Sequential experimental design chooses its next observation by its current belief and is not thereby biased. | Active |
| [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) | The topology of a support graph does not fix how a conclusion should be revised when one of its supports fails: two records with the same edges can carry evidence of different strength and call for different revisions | A6's compensating-evidence case ([CASE-089](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-089.md)), granted against reading [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) as saying a graph of justifications is enough. Two pieces of evidence support H in both worlds. Discount the first, and posterior odds are 20:1 in one world and 1.1:1 in the other. `rests_on` and `grounds` record that support exists, not how much. | Active |
| [CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md) | Two inquiry histories can agree on every current conclusion and still call for different revisions of it, so a current marginal belief is not a sufficient state for updating on evidence about what it depended on | A5's central claim, made exact by A8's construction ([CASE-093](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-093.md)) and checked here. Two joint distributions over a hypothesis H and a condition C share P(H) = 0.9; learning C = 1 sends one to 1.0 and the other to 0.8. Keeping only the marginal merges histories that need different updates. It does not say a full posterior falls short ([CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)), or that a dependency graph is the fix ([CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-299](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-299.md) | Decision sufficiency, historical accountability and correctness are three properties of a record of inquiry, and each can hold while the other two fail | A8's "small mathematical structure", with A5's "Epistemic traceability and epistemic sufficiency are different properties". Shown by construction: a sufficient posterior without history ([CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md)), a perfectly accountable record that is wrong ([CASE-084](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-084.md)), a current marginal that is right and cannot be revised ([CASE-093](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-093.md)). [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) and [CLAIM-190](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-190.md) hold neighbouring points about measuring an argument. This names the three predicates so the others can say which they mean. | Active |
| [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md) | A state sufficient for a family of decisions under a model makes the rest of an inquiry's history worthless for those decisions, and it can stop being sufficient when a source is discredited, the model is revised or the decisions change | A10's answer to the owner's U10, with A8's fourth case and A10's normal constructions ([CASE-082](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-082.md), [CASE-087](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-087.md)). Under a fixed, correctly specified model a sufficient posterior makes the history redundant for those decisions. The same sample mean that sufficed cannot say which reading remains when one instrument is discredited, or test a mixture. Sufficiency was always relative to the model and the family. [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) says the same of individuation by target; this says it of a retained state over time. | Active |
| [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md) | Equivalence under feasible tests can be much coarser than statistical equivalence: there are ensembles almost disjoint from uniform that no polynomial-size test tells apart from it, and efficiently samplable ensembles of this kind exist if pseudorandom generators do | A15's witness for "Complexity changes what we mean by an observable", which the owner asked to have developed at U15, corrected by the reading of Goldreich (NOTE of 2026-10-15). [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) says agreement on a restricted probe family is coarser than identity; feasibility gives a restriction that is forced, not chosen. The separation itself is unconditional: a counting argument gives ensembles supported on at most 2^(n/2) strings that no circuit of size 2^(n/8) tells from uniform. Only an efficiently samplable witness needs an assumption, and a secure pseudorandom generator supplies one. All of it is asymptotic, about ensembles indexed by n. | Active |
| [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) | A rendering can keep a distinction recoverable in principle and make it infeasible to recover: if pseudorandom generators exist, a uniformly random bit can be encoded so that an unbounded receiver recovers it except with probability at most 2⁻⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾, while no efficient receiver does non-negligibly better than chance | A14's first failure mode, computational inaccessibility, and A18's fourth candidate: "Recoverable in principle ≠ recoverable within budget." [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) shows a garbling can help a bounded receiver. This is the other direction: a nearly lossless rendering can defeat every efficient one. The construction is the record's, from [CLAIM-302](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-302.md)'s witness; A18 asked for one and warned against "a vague appeal to an inverse being hard". | Active |
| [CLAIM-305](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md) | Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient | The owner's LEGO monograph says, in Part I (chapters 4, 6, 7, 9, the Overview and "Definitions and Theorems"), that blow-up "restores identifiability", "introduces new observables" and makes the Fisher information non-degenerate, and maps it onto splitting a LEGO bin. The pulled-back model is p(x \| π(u)), a function of u only through π(u), so every point of the exceptional divisor gives the distribution of the singular point. In p(x \| a, b) = N(ab, 1), the chart a = u, b = uv gives mean u²v and a Fisher matrix of zero all along u = 0. Splitting a bin is refining the observable, which can separate states. [MOM-CLM-099](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-099.md) records that the monograph uses "blow-up" in three senses; this records why the analogy cannot hold in any of them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) says when a distinction is real enough to name. Its evidence grows with the number of copies. The parable says when a distinction must be built to act in time: a single brick among similar ones. Expected search falls as copies grow. The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-309](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-309.md) | How good a mixture is and how discriminable it is from its diluent come apart: under linear mixing a smoothie's distance from milk only shrinks as milk is added, so a preference that rises and then falls with milk is over the ratio and cannot be a d′, and the signal-detection reading of the owner's smoothie line reverses one of its directions | The smoothie note in the owner's LEGO monograph reads the owner's line ([CASE-096](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-096.md)) as signal detection. Milk is the noise, "Less Good" is d′ falling as the mixture approaches milk, and "More Good" is d′ rising as a little milk is added. Under linear mixing the mixture's taste is (1 − f)s + f·m, and its distance from milk is (1 − f)\|s − m\|. That falls monotonically from the first drop, so discriminability from milk cannot rise and then fall. The note's own first model is right: goodness is a single-peaked function of the ratio, which is a preference, not a discriminability. [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md) found the same kind of reversal in the formal reading of the LEGO parable. MOM's record never mentions the smoothie note. | Active |
| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) | Sorting schemes over objects with determinate properties never conflict as descriptions, since the product of any sortings refines them all; they conflict as arrangements, since a fixed number of bins realizes one partition, and which costs least depends on what is searched for and on what stands out within a bin | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |
| [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) | A search cut off before an exhaustive pass can establish absence when the arrangement certifies that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item: a sorted table answers non-membership in a logarithmic number of probes, and the Threshold Algorithm stops early with its answer proved, so absence needs a certificate about the remainder, not exhaustion; similarity search in high dimension is where no such certificate exists | Filed at the owner's request, from the database readings set against [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry: presence by one find, absence "only by exhausting the collection". Sorted order and the Threshold Algorithm each establish absence from part of the collection, because the arrangement bounds what the rest can hold. That meets [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s own defeat condition, and the claim is conceded: [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) restates it. Where the arrangement gives no bound, as in similarity search in high dimension, [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry stands. | Active |
| [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" asserts operational unavailability, that the item will not be put to use before the deadline, not absence: a search that fails by the deadline establishes unavailability outright, and licenses absence only with a certificate that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item, from exhaustion, from an invariant of the arrangement, or from a closed-world default | Restates [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) at the owner's request, after [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) showed that absence can be established without exhausting a collection. The owner's own wording in [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md), "it may as well not be there", is hyperbole for operational availability ([TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md)), not a claim about inventory. Read so, the rule reports an outcome and needs no default. [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s analysis survives as the account of the literal reading: what a failed search must be joined with before it licenses absence. The gap between the two readings is [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s Bayes term, and it matters when the statement is passed to someone who will act on presence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-318](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-318.md) | Within a shared observational scenario, exact structure-preserving symmetries are the invertible members of a nested family of stochastic transports, and among Markov kernels between finite sets the invertible ones are the permutation matrices, so the invertible core is the relabellings, a groupoid in which objects joined by an arrow have isomorphic automorphism groups | Split from [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the nesting and its invertible core, stated on their own so that their warrant can be. A110 §25 nests exact symmetries inside structure-compatible transports inside stochastic communicative transports, within a shared scenario, and the exact symmetries are the invertible ones. For Markov kernels between finite sets, a stochastic matrix with a stochastic inverse is a permutation matrix, because a nonnegative matrix with a nonnegative inverse is monomial, so the invertible core is the relabellings. In that groupoid an invertible u : A → B gives Aut(A) ≅ Aut(B), which corrects A198 §8. It does not say what symmetries are for: that they supply the yardstick for non-symmetric transports is [CLAIM-103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-103.md)'s, and interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-319](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-319.md) | Over a scenario of n contexts in an odd cycle, changing the support of one context takes the contextual fraction from 1 to 0 while the other n − 1 contexts and every marginal are kept exactly, at a weighted observational distortion of 1/n, so within a scenario the fraction's Lipschitz constant against that distortion is at least n; and any change of global extension needs a contextual model on one side | Split from [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the derivation that claim called "decisive and checkable", stated on its own. For odd n, an n-cycle of ±1 observables in which every context anticorrelates is strongly contextual; making one context correlate gives a model with a global distribution. The two agree on n − 1 contexts and on every marginal, differ by total variation 1 in the last, and so lie at weighted D_obs = 1/n with contextual fractions 1 and 0. For n = 3 it is [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md) with one observable relabelled. It answers how small the local change can be; it says nothing about whether any data are contextual. | Active |
| [CLAIM-320](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-320.md) | Within one fixed measurement scenario, two no-signalling empirical models can agree on all but one of their contexts and on every single-observable marginal while their contextual fractions are 1 and 0, so keeping most local judgement distributions does not fix their global compatibility | Split from [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the possibility that claim's headline needs, shown by the pair it lost and recovered in [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). On the cover {AB, BC, AC} with binary outcomes, the parity triangle at 1/2 per allowed outcome is no-signalling and strongly contextual, with contextual fraction 1. Change only S_AC to {(0,0), (1,1)}: two contexts and every marginal are unchanged, and the model now extends to a global distribution, with fraction 0. It is an existence result by construction, and the weights are stipulated. It does not say reconstruction chains do this, which is [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)'s thesis and interpretive, and the context that changes moves by a total-variation distance of 1. | Active |
| [CLAIM-323](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-323.md) | Where source and rendering are experiments about one common situation, a rendering that depends on the situation other than through the source is not a garbling of it and can be incomparable with it in Blackwell's order: with Z uniform on {1, 2, 3}, a source that tells whether Z = 1 and a rendering that tells whether Z = 3 each have the lower 0–1 risk on one of the problems of saying whether Z = 1 and whether Z = 3, so neither dominates | Split from [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the worked case that objection uses, stated on its own so that its warrant can be. Over a common situation Z uniform on three values, U reports whether Z = 1 and V whether Z = 3. V is not a garbling of U, since given U = 0 it still varies with Z, and the risks on "say whether Z = 3" (0 from V, 1/3 from U) and "say whether Z = 1" (the reverse) show neither experiment dominates. It is an existence result by construction. It does not say this is the normal translation case, which is [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md)'s reading and is interpretive. | Active |
| [CLAIM-325](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-325.md) | The behavioural data the record has read show no contextuality proper: none of the five kinds of data Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala re-analyse is contextual, Wang et al. test none of their 90 language systems for it, and no documented test of pragmatic or meaning judgements finds it at adequate power | Split from [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical premise of that objection's dilemma, which [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) conceded. Dzhafarov, Zhang and Kujala ([LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md), read in [NOTE-235](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-235.md)) find none of five kinds of behavioural data contextual, two of them previously published as contextual; Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky and Cervantes ([LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md)) report signalling in 69 of 90 language systems and test none for contextuality; [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) collects the documented tests on elicited judgements and finds no contextual pragmatic data. It is scoped: [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) records a reliable positive result on instructed matching, so "none in behavioural data" is too broad, and the absence is [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md)'s working hypothesis, not a proof that such data cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md) | Measuring every relevant variable is necessary but not sufficient for a Granger-causal analysis to say anything about interventions: the intervention must also be an isolated exogenous change and no influence may act within one sampling step, and then Granger noncausality implies no intervention effect and the effect is identified from the observational predictor, but a Granger-causal relation is still only potentially causal | The record's answer to [NOTE-010](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-010.md)'s C5, "if all relevant variables are measured, Granger- and Pearl-type analyses coincide", which the ΦID review asserts without conditions. Eichler and Didelez ([THEORY-704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md)) give sufficient conditions, and complete measurement is one of them. A two-variable process with nothing hidden shows it is not enough: a acts on b within one step, a is Granger-noncausal for b, and setting a(t) changes the mean of b(t + 1) by ργ. Checked by hand and by simulation. | Active |
| [CLAIM-334](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md) | Granger causation from a macro variable to the micro variables it supervenes on, Seth's downward Granger causation, is not evidence of a macro-to-micro intervention effect, even with every micro variable measured: supervenience leaves no intervention on the macro variable that holds its micro base fixed at the same time | Seth measures downward causation as Granger causation from the flock's centre of mass to each boid, and calls it "ontologically innocent" ([THEORY-703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-703.md)). The record files the boundary so that the stronger reading has an address. If M(t) = f(m(t)), setting M(t) means changing m(t), so the intervention Eichler and Didelez's Assumption 2.3(i) requires does not exist ([THEORY-704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-704.md)). Measuring every boid does not help, by [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md). | Active |
| [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md) | Transfer entropy measures directed predictive improvement, not information flow: as a conditional mutual information it is the source's unique information about the target's next value plus its synergy with the target's past, so it can credit a source with a bit the source carries only jointly and read zero from sources that jointly fix the target, and conditioning on more series does not remove the synergy | The record's position on whether transfer entropy measures information flow. James, Barnett and Crutchfield show it does not, if flow is information attributable to the source alone ([THEORY-707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-707.md)). Williams and Beer's decomposition shows why, for any partial information decomposition satisfying the consistency equations ([THEORY-712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-712.md)). Both papers' examples were recomputed exactly. This is a different failure from [CLAIM-333](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-333.md)'s, prediction against intervention. It leaves transfer entropy standing as a predictive quantity. | Active |
